cells.tense: What was carried quietly has been seen and named, and here you are with it.
cells.ask: Retire a routine kept going since the sacrifice ended — a weekly call, a small duty nobody is waiting on — for one week, with no replacement.
cells.core:
What you carried a while has been seen and named. That is the thing complete: a private effort turned visible, no defense required, no translation needed for anyone at the table. You can sit where people pass things back and forth without first explaining the shape of it.

A load held correctly is still hard to release. You can keep tending the same routine long after the need that started it ended, and call that loyalty. Retire one of them — not the whole meaning, just one weekly thing that began around the same stretch. Let it go quiet a week and watch what happens when it is not kept up. Most often nothing topples, and the people beside you are fine.

cells.tense: You are already living at the far end of the sacrifice, waiting on a thank-you not yet said.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Split this week's obligations into three rows — freely agreed, quietly added, and done to dodge being seen as less — then strike the third.
cells.core:
The work keeps being arranged for a moment that has not arrived, and anything short of that moment reads as unfinished. Every week a little extra gets added to something already done, in case it turns out not to count. What is actually happening now gets spent on a verdict still to come.

It goes heavy fast, and it goes clean just as fast. Take this week's obligations and split them three ways: what you freely said yes to, what quietly got added, what you do so nobody thinks less of you. Strike the third. What remains is honest work, and honest work can be left standing on its own.

cells.tense: The giving is behind you, and you are at the doorway still unsure it counted.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Hold one thing you gave as yours to carry, and stop checking whether it registered with anyone.
cells.core:
Something was paid earlier, and it is not being counted here — not from modesty, more that the payment stopped being yours to hold. You keep half in the doorway, listening for confirmation it was wanted. The warmth has not gone anywhere. You stand outside it, keeping the question open.

Owning what was paid is what lets the rest arrive. Take one thing you gave — a year, a stretch of time, a comfort you went without. Hold it as yours, near enough to touch, and stop checking whether it registered with anyone. Nobody is being asked for anything here. The point is to stop holding the door.

cells.tense: You hold each of them steady and have not once called what you do by a name.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: For one week, note what you quietly keep steady for someone — hours, costs, arrangements — and count it as tending.
cells.core:
The people near you know exactly where they stand. That has been kept true a long while — the calendar moved, the cup filled, the difficult room made easy before anyone had to ask. The one keeping it level has not described it as upkeep. So far as you tell it, it is simply what you do.

The ground does not hold itself. For one week, note down what you are quietly keeping steady — a person, a load, an arrangement — and count the hours and costs as tending. No mailing it anywhere, no collecting thanks. Not credit. Just the one carrying it knowing where they stand, the way you know it for everybody else.
